subject: comparing fits vs. each other and simulations

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: comparing fits vs. each other and simulations
parts:
It'd be nice in R to be able to do something like this:

compare(c(fit1,fit2), sim, c("alpha","beta"))

to compare two (or more) fits, with a single (optional)
named list of "true" values, and an optional list of
a subset of parameters (like in print or traceplot in RStan).

I don't yet know enough about what I want to put into either
output or a visualization to make a feature request out of
this for RStan or PyStan (or shinyStan).

-Bob

Definitely compare() for posterior predictive distributions of multiple models against the observed outcome. But comparing the posterior distributions of parameters across models only makes goods sense when the models are nested, which we can't enforce but we could doc.

Ben

in a Poisson vs. negative binomial, or even predictions in
two wildly different models.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] comparing fits vs. each other and simulations
parts:
On Sunday, March 1, 2015 at 7:48:59 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'm not sure what you mean by "nested."
One model is a special case or limiting case of the other

I'm imagining
something where, for instance, I use two different priors or
different hyperprior distributions
Might make sense if the parameters that you are comparing are a priori independent of the priors that are different.

or maybe look at means
in a Poisson vs. negative binomial
That works since Poisson is a limiting case of the negative binomial

or even predictions in
two wildly different models.

For posterior predictive distributions, definitely. But the parameters wouldn't be comparable in wildly different models, even if they have the same "role" (e.g. alpha is an intercept, beta is a slope, etc.) because their interpretations would be different in wildly different models.

Ben
